'''''Alyssum montanum''''' is a species of [[flowering plant]] belonging to the family [[Brassicaceae]].<ref name="POWO">{{cite web |title=Alyssum montanum L. {{!}} Plants of the World Online {{!}} Kew Science |url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:277653-1 |website=Plants of the World Online |access-date=25 January 2021 |language=en}}</ref> It is an evergreen, prostrate perennial with small, hairy, greyish [[Leaf|leaves]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Alyssum montanum {{!}} mountain madwort/RHS Gardening|url=http://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/1032/Alyssum-montanum/Details|access-date=2021-04-27|website=www.rhs.org.uk|language=en-gb}}</ref> It typically grows to 10-15 centimeters tall and 30-45 centimeters across.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Plant Profile for Alyssum montanum Mountain Gold - Mountain Gold Alyssum Perennial|url=http://www.perennials.com/plants/alyssum-montanum-mountain-gold.html|access-date=2021-04-28|website=www.perennials.com}}</ref> It produces tiny, yellow, fragrant [[flower]]s from May to July.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Alyssum montanum - Beth Chatto's Plants & Gardens|url=https://www.bethchatto.co.uk/shop-by-other/a-z-plants/alyssum-montanum.htm|access-date=2021-04-28|website=www.bethchatto.co.uk|archive-date=2023-10-14|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231014160343/https://www.bethchatto.co.uk/shop-by-other/a-z-plants/alyssum-montanum.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref> These flowers are typically 4-6 centimeters across and borne in dense [[raceme]]s.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Home|url=https://www.alpinegardensociety.net/|access-date=2021-04-28|website=Alpine Garden Society|language=en}}</ref>

It is native to [[France]], [[Switzerland]], and [[Germany]].<ref name="POWO" /> It grows best in full sun with good drainage, and is [[Drought tolerance|drought tolerant]] once established.<ref name=":0" /> It is suitable for [[Hardiness zone|USDA hardiness zones]] 3–9, but may be susceptible to [[aphid]]s and [[root rot]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=StackPath|url=https://www.gardeningknowhow.com/ornamental/flowers/alyssum/growing-mountain-alyssum.htm|access-date=2021-04-28|website=www.gardeningknowhow.com|date=11 September 2013 }}</ref>
